findings.label: Suppliers with Current Red Flags
findings.detail: 5 current suppliers have Companies House compliance issues (historical payments were made before breaches started)

findings.label: Suspected Split Payments
findings.detail: 229 instances of 3+ payments just below approval thresholds in the same week
findings.context_note: Split payment detection has a high false-positive rate. Batch processing, staged invoices, and legitimate recurring payments can all trigger this pattern. FOI request for procurement approval chain recommended before drawing conclusions.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 2217 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: NHS Campus Reprov. Phase 1 spent 2.3x their monthly average in March (£1.1M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 15 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Compass Minerals Uk Ltd (3.8 day avg, 1022 payments, £5.4M)

findings.label: Benford's Law Analysis
findings.detail: Digit distribution across 279,239 transactions shows χ²=13198.59 (statistically significant due to large sample size), but max digit deviation is only 4.1% — within the normal range for UK council spending patterns. No practical evidence of fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 279,239+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (4.1%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 279,239 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 2.52% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=279,239.

findings.label: Weak Competition Indicators
findings.detail: 9 contracts show signs of limited competition (short tender periods or rapid award). Top: GB-Stafford: TPPL Staffordshire County Council NEP (£2.0M)
findings.context_note: Contracts Finder does not publish bid counts. These flags use proxy signals: tender periods under 14 days and awards within 7 days of deadline. Short timelines may have legitimate explanations (framework call-offs, urgency).

findings.label: High-Risk Councillors
findings.detail: 12 councillors scored 'high risk' in integrity assessment across 36 data sources. Most common flags: undeclared interests, supplier conflicts, and company compliance issues.

key_findings.title: 10 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Crown Oil Ltd — every 4.1 days (95 payments, £161.6K)

key_findings.title: LIVING AMBITIONS LTD: 4113 transactions totalling £10.0M
key_findings.description: Averaging £2.4K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier

key_findings.title: 1 service categories with a single supplier
key_findings.description: Top: Broad Oak Properties Ltd — sole winner in 'Construction work for multi-dwelling bui' (2 contracts, £11.7M). Category monopolies may indicate market failure or specification bias.

key_findings.title: AI DOGE covers 49% of £926.6M GOV.UK outturn
key_findings.description: Spending >£500 threshold means smaller transactions are excluded. Largest gaps: Education services, Highways and transport services, Children Social Care. This is expected — not a data quality issue.
